description: baseline validated locally; geomean benchmark captured before launching workers

Prototype a CUDA C++ blocked panel QR implementation for n=1024 through n=4096 using shared-memory reductions for panel norms and batched trailing updates, targeting large-shape latency instead of PyTorch launch overhead.
cuSOLVER extension prototype failed at import because torch extension ninja was unavailable in the wrapped build environment; abandoning library path for custom CUDA C++ per brief steering.
cuSOLVER geqrf extension built after exposing venv ninja on PATH but failed leaderboard banned-construct scan due explicit CUDA stream/cusolver stream usage.
custom one-block Householder prototype failed to build because CUDA kernel source was supplied as cpp_sources, so c++ compiled __global__ launch syntax.
custom CUDA source split compiled nvcc side but pybind stub lacked a C++ declaration for geqrf_custom_cuda.
custom one-block Householder QR built and passed official test shapes, but differential benchmark-shape guard was orders too slow and was interrupted after ~26 minutes.
valid hybrid custom CUDA Householder path for n<=352 with PyTorch geqrf fallback above that; correctness guards pass but geomean regresses to 122557 us because n=176/352 one-block kernels are slow.

restricted custom one-block Householder QR to n=32 and used torch.geqrf for n>32; validates but still slower than baseline at 118271 us, with n=32 custom launch not offsetting extension overhead/noise.

Brief exhausted. A custom CUDA one-block Householder QR for n<=352 validated but regressed badly (122557 us), and restricting it to n=32 still regressed (118271 us vs 116406 baseline). Full large-shape custom QR passed test shapes but was too slow for the differential guard; cuSOLVER/cuBLAS-style library paths were either banned by stream guards or impractical. Profile of final n=32 route saved; NCU shows the tiny custom kernel is launch/occupancy limited, so next briefs should avoid one-block geqr2 for large panels and prefer structural shortcuts like worker-1's rank/upper routes or true multi-block blocked trailing-update designs.

Extend 90cd3e5's triangular fast path to other active benchmark shapes: profile shortcut overhead, then add CUDA C++ low-overhead exact detectors for identity, diagonal, zero, or trailing-zero-column batches that preserve current QR output semantics and fall back to geqrf on any uncertainty.

Replace Python all().item upper/tail detectors with one CUDA C++ structure scan returning flags; validates but regresses to 114371.813 us because scanning all n>=512 dense batches adds overhead compared with parent 90cd3e5.

Gate the CUDA C++ tail-zero detector to candidate rank-def/large shapes while keeping parent Python upper detector; validates and improves over broad CUDA scan but still trails parent at 114151.030 us.

Optimize CUDA C++ detector to scan only trailing columns for rank-def batches; validation passed and benchmark improved to 113961.707 us, slightly faster than parent 90cd3e5 by reducing rankdef detection overhead.

Add a scalar sentinel check before launching CUDA tail scan to avoid dense detector work; validates but benchmark regresses to 114039.195 us versus tail-only 113961.707, likely due synchronization/item overhead.
Add exact all-zero batch fast path before upper/tail routes; validates but regresses to 114126.411 us because active benchmark set has no zero batches and detector sync adds overhead.

Brief exhausted. Best result is commit 6e5f90f6 with linalg/qr_v2=113961.707 us, a small improvement over parent 90cd3e5's 113986.585 by replacing full-matrix Python tail-zero checks with a CUDA C++ detector that scans only trailing columns. Broad CUDA structure scan (114371.813), sentinel precheck (114039.195), and zero-batch fast path (114126.411) all validated but regressed due synchronization/detector overhead or no matching active shapes. Profile saved for 6e5f90f6; remaining bottleneck is still torch/geqrf work, not detector code, so next briefs should target new exact structural shortcuts with active shapes or real QR compute reductions.

Explore a separate large-shape rankdef shortcut for active n=1024 and n=2048: detect exact zero trailing columns for rank 3n/4, run QR only on the active leading width with custom CUDA C++ packing/unpacking or a reduced-width route, preserve fallback to torch.geqrf, and benchmark detector plus reduced-width overhead against full geqrf.

Add CUDA C++ zero-tail detector for n=1024/2048 plus reduced-width torch.geqrf route when every matrix is exact rank 3n/4; validation passed but benchmark regressed to 116422.410 us because active benchmark set lacks homogeneous exact rankdef 1024/2048 batches.

Extend large rankdef detector to split n=1024 mixed batches per matrix, running reduced-width geqrf on exact zero-tail matrices and full geqrf on others; validation passed, mixed 1024 improves but overall regresses to 116279.427 us due overhead and no 512 path.

Gate per-matrix large rankdef split to n=1024 batch=60 only; validation passed and mixed 1024 remains faster, but overall still regresses to 116283.283 us because dense 1024 detector overhead and absent 512 shortcut dominate.

Brief exhausted. Large-shape zero-tail rankdef shortcuts for n=1024/2048 did not beat baseline alone. Homogeneous n=1024/2048 exact-rank route validated but regressed to 116422.410 because no active benchmark has all matrices zero-tail at those sizes. Per-matrix n=1024 mixed split improved that one shape (~218.4 ms vs ~221 ms) but overall still regressed to 116279-116283 because only 1/60 active mixed matrices had exact zero tail and detector/indexing overhead dominates. Profile saved for final mixed-only commit b5d764b2; next work should stack with the stronger n=512 rankdef path or target non-exact nearrank structure, not isolated large exact zero-tail routing.

Combine 22ac853 with donor 9361695 surgically: start from 22ac853, preserve the n=512 split-rankdef path unchanged, and port only the n=1024 mixed exact-zero-tail per-matrix reduced-width dispatch behind the narrow batch=60,n=1024 mixed guard; keep a cheap zero-tail predicate so normal mixed matrices fall through, and keep only if mixed-1024 gain survives and total geomean beats 112668.376.

Combined parent 22ac853 n=512 split-rankdef CUDA path unchanged with donor 9361695 n=1024,batch=60 per-matrix exact zero-tail reduced-width dispatch; validation passed and benchmark geomean improved to 112545.069 us, beating target 112668.376.

Combine brief succeeded. Starting from 22ac853, preserved the n=512 split-rankdef CUDA path unchanged and ported only donor 9361695's n=1024,batch=60 per-matrix exact zero-tail reduced-width dispatch. Candidate acfe5ec7 validates and benchmarks at 112545.069 us, beating the 112668.376 target and improving the mixed-1024 shape to about 217.6 ms while retaining the 512 rankdef win. Profile saved for acfe5ec7; remaining profile hints still point at low-occupancy geqr2-style 512 kernel and torch.geqrf-dominated dense shapes.

Combine 59e270 clustered n=512 best with acfe5ec7's n=1024 donor only if dispatch predicates stay disjoint: port the narrow batch=60,n=1024 mixed exact-zero-tail reduced-width path behind an exact shape and tail detector, leave all n=512 clustered and rankdef dispatch and kernels byte-identical unless compile integration requires otherwise, and keep only if geomean beats 103221.174 with no per-case regression on clustered n=512, rankdef n=512, or existing n=1024 dense cases.

Integrated donor n=1024 mixed exact-zero-tail path into 59e270's CUDA extension; validation passed and mixed-1024 improved, but geomean 104056.001 misses 103221.174 target with n=512 rankdef/clustered per-case slower than desired, likely from compile/integration perturbation.

Isolate the donor n=1024 batch=60 exact-zero-tail path in a second CUDA extension to keep parent n=512 code byte-identical; validation passed but geomean is 104044.885 us, missing the 103221.174 target.
Add a cheap CUDA sentinel precheck before the n=1024 exact-zero-tail scan; validation passed and geomean improved to 103475.181 us, but still misses the 103221.174 combine target.
Try sentinel-only n=1024 exact-zero-tail routing without the full tail scan; validation passed but geomean regressed to 103501.483 us versus sentinel+scan, still missing target.

Combine brief exhausted. Best candidate is 762b4c9c with isolated n=1024 donor extension plus CUDA sentinel-gated full tail scan, validating at linalg/qr_v2=103475.181 us. It improves over naive isolate/inlined attempts (104044-104056 us) but misses parent target 103221.174; sentinel-only was valid but slower at 103501.483. n=512 parent kernels were preserved, and profile saved at /home/shadeform/breval-target/problems/linalg/qr_v2/autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-03-04-02-qrv2_kernel_languages_yxiwb80jg/worker-2-brief-4-best-762b4c9ce17e0a98db5beaf46f2c52e590018a4f.ncu.txt.

Surgically combine 52846b2 with only 18dec0c's clustered 128x64 tail-sample detector: preserve CLUSTER_RANK=256, band and rankdef detection, mixed-band compaction, and all fallback dispatch; reject if any mixed-band or rankdef bucket regresses, and keep only if clustered overhead drops enough for total geomean to beat 102840.243.

Surgically port donor 18dec0c's 128x64 clustered tail-sample detector and 0.01 threshold into parent 52846b2 while preserving CLUSTER_RANK=256, rankdef/band detection, mixed-band compaction, and fallback dispatch; validation passed and geomean improved to 102748.878 us, beating 102840.243.

Combine brief succeeded. Starting from 52846b2, ported only 18dec0c's clustered detector change: 128x64 post-boundary tail sample and 0.01 threshold. CLUSTER_RANK=256, rankdef and band detectors, mixed-band compaction, and fallbacks remain intact. Candidate 9b003b2e validates and benchmarks at linalg/qr_v2=102748.878 us, beating the 102840.243 target; profile saved at /home/shadeform/breval-target/problems/linalg/qr_v2/autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-03-04-02-qrv2_kernel_languages_yxiwb80jg/worker-2-brief-5-iteration-0-9b003b2eed2749bdac9120a9fec48af667c7e5b9.ncu.txt.

Explore an n=512 rowscale structural shortcut from 9b003b2: profile active rowscale cases, add a conservative detector for deterministic per-row logspace scaling, and try an isolated row-normalized QR path that explicitly maps results back to the original scale and passes validation; preserve unchanged fallback for band, cluster, rankdef, dense, and unknown cases, and keep only if geomean beats 102748.878.

Add a conservative n=512 rowscale detector plus truncated-row custom Householder path with ROWSCALE_RANK=384 and mixed-batch compaction; validation passed and geomean improved to 102473.876 us, beating parent 102748.878.
Lower ROWSCALE_RANK to 320 for the n=512 rowscale truncated-row QR path; build passed but validation failed on rowscale with R-Q.T@A residual 0.171 > 0.0649, so this cutoff is too aggressive.
Try intermediate ROWSCALE_RANK=352 for the n=512 rowscale truncated QR path; build passed but validation failed on rowscale with R-Q.T@A residual 0.0947 > 0.0654.
Try ROWSCALE_RANK=368 for rowscale truncated QR; build passed but validation failed narrowly on rowscale with residual 0.0695 > 0.065, so cutoff is still too aggressive.
